issues.legal_issue: Leasing plant and machinery after the firm had ceased its manufacturing business and the assets had ceased to be commercial assets did not constitute carrying on a business.
material_facts: The firm had manufactured ribbons and laces using its plant and machinery.
A company acquired the land and buildings where the plant and machinery were installed, leaving the firm unable to use those assets for manufacturing.
The firm ceased manufacturing and was left with plant and machinery that it no longer required and that had ceased to be commercial assets in its hands.
The firm leased the plant and machinery to the company for annual rent.
issues.conclusion: The letting of the plant and machinery was not business within the meaning of section 2(5) of the Excess Profits Tax Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(5) includes trade, commerce, manufacture and an adventure in the nature of trade, but business ordinarily connotes a real, substantial and systematic or organised course of activity with a set purpose. Whether an activity is business depends on the facts and ordinary conceptions of business; even an isolated transaction may qualify if it clearly bears the indicia of trade. The Court relied on Commissioner of Income-tax v. Shaw Wallace & Co. and Inland Revenue Commissioners v. Broadway Car Co., Ltd., distinguished Commissioner of Excess Profits Tax, Bombay City v. Shri Lakshmi Silk Mills Ltd., and noted that sections 12(3) and 12(4) of the Indian Income-tax Act recognise that letting plant or machinery may produce income under “other sources” rather than business.

rule.if: excess_profits_tax_assessment and manufacturing_business_ended and assets_ceased_to_be_commercial and assets_leased_for_rent

predicates.excess_profits_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerned assessment of profits tax on a taxpayer.
predicates.manufacturing_business_ended: The taxpayer stopped its manufacturing activity rather than temporarily suspending part of an ongoing business.
predicates.assets_ceased_to_be_commercial: The taxpayer's plant or machinery was no longer used or available for use in its former business.
predicates.assets_leased_for_rent: The taxpayer let the plant or machinery to another person in return for rent.

issues.definition: When a profits-tax assessment concerns a taxpayer whose manufacturing business has ended, whose assets have ceased to be commercial assets, and who leases those assets for rent, the letting is not treated as business.

issues.legal_issue: The power to make anti-avoidance adjustments in an excess-profits-tax assessment depended on the taxpayer carrying on a business to which the tax applied during the relevant period.
material_facts: During the relevant accounting periods, the firm had stopped manufacturing ribbons and laces.
The firm could not use the plant and machinery because it no longer had rights to the land and buildings where they were installed.
The firm's only relevant activity was leasing the plant and machinery, which was not business.
The revenue used the anti-avoidance provision to seek aggregation of income earned through associated firms with the firm's income.
issues.conclusion: The anti-avoidance provision could not be invoked, and aggregating the associated firms' income with the firm's income was not valid.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4 and 5 of the Excess Profits Tax Act contemplate a business carried on by the taxpayer whose profits are subject to the tax. Proof that the taxpayer carried on a business of the kind covered by section 5 during the relevant accounting period is a condition precedent to an inquiry and adjustments under section 10-A. Since the firm had no such business, the question whether the transactions were undertaken to avoid tax did not arise.

rule.if: excess_profits_tax_assessment and anti_avoidance_aggregation_sought and not taxpayer_carried_on_taxable_business

predicates.excess_profits_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerned assessment of profits tax on a taxpayer.
predicates.anti_avoidance_aggregation_sought: The revenue sought to adjust the taxpayer's assessment by aggregating income associated with transactions involving other entities.
predicates.taxpayer_carried_on_taxable_business: The taxpayer carried on a business of the kind subject to the profits tax during the relevant accounting period.

issues.definition: If the revenue seeks aggregation in a profits-tax assessment and the taxpayer did not carry on a business subject to that tax during the relevant period, the aggregation is not valid.

issues.legal_issue: A partner's share of income from an associated firm's activity could not be included in the taxpayer's assessment through an anti-avoidance adjustment when the taxpayer carried on no business subject to the tax.
material_facts: The revenue sought to aggregate income of associated firms with the taxpayer firm's income under the anti-avoidance provision.
The taxpayer firm's manufacturing business had ended, and its leasing of plant and machinery was not business.

The Court answered the question concerning inclusion of a partner's share of the associated firm's income in the taxpayer's assessment in the negative as a necessary corollary of its conclusion that the anti-avoidance provision could not be invoked.
issues.conclusion: The partner's share of income could not be included in the taxpayer firm's assessment under the anti-avoidance provision.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 5 and 10-A of the Excess Profits Tax Act require a taxpayer to carry on a business to which the Act applies before the anti-avoidance adjustment power can be used. Because that condition was not met, the attempted aggregation, including the partner's share, could not be made.

rule.if: excess_profits_tax_assessment and partner_income_aggregation_sought and not taxpayer_carried_on_taxable_business

predicates.excess_profits_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerned assessment of profits tax on a taxpayer.
predicates.partner_income_aggregation_sought: The revenue sought to include in the taxpayer's assessment a partner's share of income earned through an associated firm.
predicates.taxpayer_carried_on_taxable_business: The taxpayer carried on a business of the kind subject to the profits tax during the relevant accounting period.

issues.definition: If the revenue seeks to include a partner's share of associated-firm income in a profits-tax assessment and the taxpayer did not carry on a business subject to that tax during the relevant period, the share cannot be included through the anti-avoidance adjustment.
